subject: refactor(ssh_dotnet): decompose Connect() into focused helpers (S3776)
body:
refactor(ssh_dotnet): decompose Connect() into focused helpers (S3776)

Extract the 267-line Connect() into a linear orchestrator + small single-purpose
helpers (TryResolveParameters / TryBuildAuthentication / TryEstablishSshConnection /
ConfigureTunnels / TryStartTerminalSession / TryCreateShellStream /
ExecuteOpeningCommand / FocusTerminalAfterConnect). Pure extraction: behaviour,
control flow, error handling, and threading are unchanged, so no deadlock/cross-thread
risk. Cognitive complexity of Connect() drops well under the limit.

S6966 (await ConnectAsync) is intentionally NOT applied here: the connect call's
threading model is load-bearing and can only be verified against a real server + UI,
so the sync connect is retained. The adapter already exposes ConnectAsync for a future
fully-async path. Not gate-blocking.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

triage.rationale: Refactors ProtocolSshDotNet.cs, a fork-specific SSH.NET protocol our fork does not have. Behavior-neutral S3776 decomposition of foreign code.
